The probability density function of a multvariate normal distrbution is defined as
$$
f_x(x)=\frac{1}{(2\pi \det(\Sigma))^d}\exp(-\frac{1}{2}(x-\mu)^T\Sigma(x-\mu))
$$

## Example 1
```{r}
library("mnormt")
mu=c(0,1)
Sigma=matrix(c(1,0.5,0.5,1),nrow=2)
base1<-seq(0,1,by=0.01)
set<-expand.grid(base1,base1)
temp<-dmnorm(set,mean=mu,varcov=Sigma)
temp2<-matrix(temp,nrow=length(base1))
persp(base1,base1,temp2,theta=30,
xlab="x",ylab="y",zlab="z",main="pdf of a multivariate normal distrbution")

base1<-seq(-5,5,by=0.01)
set<-expand.grid(base1,base1)
temp<-dmnorm(set,mean=mu,varcov=Sigma)
temp2<-matrix(temp,nrow=length(base1))
contour(base1,base1,temp2,xlim=c(-5,5),ylim=c(-5,5))

eigen(Sigma)
val<- eigen(Sigma)$values
vec<- eigen(Sigma)$vectors
temp1<-val[1]
temp2<-val[2]
sqrt(temp1/temp2);sqrt(temp2/temp1)

y<-rmnorm(1000,mean=mu,varcov=Sigma)
head(y)
plot(y,main="scatter plot")
```

## Example 2
```{r}
g1<-qnorm(0.995,0,1)
print(g1)

temp<-matrix(0,nrow=50)
library("mnormt")
alpha<-0.995
for (i in 1:50){
temp[i]<-qchisq(alpha,i)
}
head(temp)
base<-seq(1,50,by=1)
length(base);length(temp)
plot(base,temp,xlab="dimension",ylab="alpha",main="Radius v.s. dimensional of the data")

f0<-dnorm(0,0,1)
f1<-dnorm(g1,0,1)
thet<-f1/f0
print(thet)

temp<-matrix(0,nrow=50)
for (i in 1:50){
temp[i]<- pchisq(-2*log(thet),i)
}
base<-seq(1,50,by=1)
plot(base,temp,
main="Probability for a standard multivariate normal for different dimension",
xlab="dimension",ylab="Probability")
```

### Proof for Part 4:
Recall that
$$
f_x(x)=\frac{1}{(2\pi \det(\Sigma))^d}\exp(-\frac{1}{2}(x-\mu)^T\Sigma(x-\mu))
$$
Assume $X\sim MN(0,I_d)$

Then we have
$$
f_x(x)=\frac{1}{(2\pi)^d}\exp(-\frac{1}{2}(x-\mu)^T(x-\mu))
$$
$$
f_x(0)=\frac{1}{(2\pi)^d}
$$
$$
\eta=\frac{f(x)}{f(0)}=\exp(-\frac{1}{2}(x^T x))=exp(-\frac{1}{2}r_d^2)
$$
$$
r_d^2=-2\log(\eta)
$$

We found that

1. ZCA-cor whitening produces the largest average componentwise cross-correlation.
2. PCA-cor whitening produces the largest compression in terms of sums of squared cross-correlation.

## Example 5
Recall that

The whitening matrix is defined as
$$
W=Q_1 \Sigma^{\frac{1}{2}}=Q_2 P^{\frac{1}{2}} V^{\frac{1}{2}}
$$
where $Q_1$, and $Q_2$ are othogonal matrix, $P=V^{\frac{1}{2}}\Sigma V^{\frac{1}{2}}$, and $V$ is the diagonal matrix containing the variances.


Cross covariance matrix $\Phi$ can be shown as
$$
\Phi=\Sigma W^T
$$

Similarly, the cross correlation matrix $\Psi$ can be shown as
$$
\Psi=V^{\frac{1}{2}}\Sigma W^T
$$

In the following, we defined a function called "diagonalmatrix" which is use to find the matrix $D^k$.
$$
A^k = P D^k P^{-1}
$$
where $D$ is the diagonal matrix of the eigenvalues of $A$, and the columns of $P$ are the corresponding eigenvectors. If $P$ is orthogonal, then $P^{-1} = P^T$. This is called the eigendecomposition of $A$.
```{r}
diagonalmatrix<-function(matrix1,power){
    d<-nrow(matrix1)
    sigmapower<-matrix(0,nrow=d,ncol=d)
    eigenvalue<-eigen(matrix1)$values
    for (i in 1:d){
        for (j in 1:d){
            if (i==j){
                sigmapower[i,j]<-eigenvalue[i]^power
            }
            else{
                sigmapower[i,j]<-0
            }
        }
    }
    return(sigmapower)
}

tester1<-matrix(c(1,0,0,1),nrow=2)
diagonalmatrix(tester1,1/2)

tester2<-matrix(c(4,1,1,3),nrow=2)
diagonalmatrix(tester2,1/2)

tester3<-matrix(c(4,1,1,1,5,1,1,1,10),nrow=3)
diagonalmatrix(tester3,1/2)

# Finding the diagonal matrix whose entries are each variance raised to the kth power
findingV<-function(matrix1,power){
    d<-nrow(matrix1)
    sigmapower<-matrix(0,nrow=d,ncol=d)
    for (i in 1:d){
        for (j in 1:d){
            if (i==j){
                sigmapower[i,j]<-matrix1[i,j]^power
            }
            else{
                sigmapower[i,j]<-0
            }
        }
    }
    return(sigmapower)
}
tester1<-matrix(c(1,0,0,1),nrow=2)
findingV(tester1,1/2)

tester2<-matrix(c(4,1,1,3),nrow=2)
findingV(tester2,1)

tester3<-matrix(c(4,1,1,1,5,1,1,1,10),nrow=3)
findingV(tester3,1/2)

# Finding a matrix A^k, for some k in Z.
findAkpower<-function(Matrix1,power){
    eigenvector<-eigen(Matrix1)$vectors
    diagon<-diagonalmatrix(Matrix1,power)
    return(eigenvector%*%diagon %*% t(eigenvector))
}
tester1<-matrix(c(1,0,0,1),nrow=2)
findAkpower(tester1,10)

tester2<-matrix(c(4,1,1,3),nrow=2)
findAkpower(tester2,4)

tester3<-matrix(c(4,1,1,1,5,1,1,1,10),nrow=3)
findAkpower(tester3,1/2)

# Finding the correlation matrix P.
findingP<-function(Sigma,power){
    temp<-findingV(Sigma,-1/2)
    P<-temp%*%Sigma%*%temp
    return(findAkpower(P,power))
}

# Finding the ZCA whitening matrix.
ZCA<-function(Sigma){
    eigenvector<-eigen(Sigma)$vectors
    temp<-diagonalmatrix(Sigma,-1/2)
    temp2<-eigenvector%*%temp%*%t(eigenvector)
    return(temp2)
}
tester1<-matrix(c(1,0,0,1),nrow=2)
ZCA(tester1)

tester2<-matrix(c(4,1,1,3),nrow=2)
ZCA(tester2)

tester3<-matrix(c(4,1,1,1,5,1,1,1,10),nrow=3)
ZCA(tester3)

# Finding the PCA whitening matrix.
PCA<-function(Sigma){
    hat<-diagonalmatrix(Sigma,-1/2)
    eigenvector<-eigen(Sigma)$vectors
    temp<- hat%*%t(eigenvector)
    return(temp)
}

tester1<-matrix(c(1,0,0,1),nrow=2)
PCA(tester1)

tester2<-matrix(c(4,1,1,3),nrow=2)
PCA(tester2)

tester3<-matrix(c(4,1,1,1,5,1,1,1,10),nrow=3)
PCA(tester3)

# Finding ZCA-cor whitening matrix.
ZCAcor<-function(Sigma){
    temp1<- findingP(Sigma,-1/2)
    temp2<- findingV(Sigma,-1/2)
    return(temp1%*%temp2)
}

tester1<-matrix(c(1,0,0,1),nrow=2)
ZCAcor(tester1)

tester2<-matrix(c(4,1,1,3),nrow=2)
ZCAcor(tester2)

tester3<-matrix(c(4,1,1,1,5,1,1,1,10),nrow=3)
ZCAcor(tester3)

# Finding PCA-cor whitening matrix.
PCAcor<-function(Matrix){
    P1<- findingP(Matrix,1)
    G1<-eigen(P1)$vectors
    the<-diagonalmatrix(P1,-1/2)
    V1<-findingV(Matrix,-1/2)
    temp<- the %*% t(G1) %*% V1
    return(temp)
}

tester1<-matrix(c(1,0,0,1),nrow=2)
PCAcor(tester1)

tester2<-matrix(c(4,1,1,3),nrow=2)
PCAcor(tester2)

tester3<-matrix(c(4,1,1,1,5,1,1,1,10),nrow=3)
PCAcor(tester3)

chole<-function(Matrix){
    upper<-chol(Matrix)
    lower<-t(upper)
    return(solve(lower))
}

tester1<-matrix(c(1,0,0,1),nrow=2)
chole(tester1)
solve(t(chole(tester1)) %*% chole(tester1))

tester2<-matrix(c(4,1,1,3),nrow=2)
chole(tester2)
solve(t(chole(tester2)) %*% chole(tester2))

tester3<-matrix(c(4,1,1,1,5,1,1,1,10),nrow=3)
chole(tester3)
solve(t(chole(tester3)) %*% chole(tester3))

crosscov<-function(Sigma,method="ZCA"){
    if (method=="ZCA"){
        W<-ZCA(Sigma)
    }
    if (method=="PCA"){
        W<-PCA(Sigma)
    }
    if (method=="ZCAcor"){
        W<-ZCAcor(Sigma)
    }
    if (method=="PCAcor"){
        W<-PCAcor(Sigma)
    }
    if (method=="Cholesky"){
        W<-chole(Sigma)
    }
    temp<-Sigma %*% t(W)
    return(temp)
}
tester1<-matrix(c(1,0,0,1),nrow=2)
crosscov(tester1,"ZCA")

tester2<-matrix(c(4,1,1,3),nrow=2)
crosscov(tester2,"PCA")

tester3<-matrix(c(4,1,1,1,5,1,1,1,10),nrow=3)
crosscov(tester3)

tester4<-matrix(c(4,1,1,3),nrow=2)
method1<-c("ZCA","PCA","ZCAcor","PCAcor","Cholesky")
p<-matrix(0,nrow=5,ncol=4)
for (i in 1:5){
    p[i,]<-as.vector(crosscov(tester4,method1[i]))
}
print(p)

crosscorr<-function(Sigma,method="ZCA"){
    if (method=="ZCA"){
        W<-ZCA(Sigma)
    }
    if (method=="PCA"){
        W<-PCA(Sigma)
    }
    if (method=="ZCAcor"){
        W<-ZCAcor(Sigma)
    }
    if (method=="PCAcor"){
        W<-PCAcor(Sigma)
    }
    if (method=="Cholesky"){
        W<-chole(Sigma)
    }
    temp<-findingV(Sigma,-1/2) %*% Sigma %*% t(W)
    return(temp)
}
tester1<-matrix(c(1,0,0,1),nrow=2)
crosscorr(tester1,"ZCA")

tester2<-matrix(c(4,1,1,3),nrow=2)
crosscorr(tester2,"PCA")

tester3<-matrix(c(4,1,1,1,5,1,1,1,10),nrow=3)
crosscorr(tester3)

tester4<-matrix(c(4,1,1,3),nrow=2)
method1<-c("ZCA","PCA","ZCAcor","PCAcor","Cholesky")
p<-matrix(0,nrow=5,ncol=4)
for (i in 1:5){
    p[i,]<-as.vector(crosscorr(tester4,method1[i]))
}
print(p)

# We are now interested in the proportion of the total variance across different whitening methods.
# The relative contribution of each element in z to explain the total variation.
ZCAprop<-function(Sigma){
    empty<-matrix(0,nrow=nrow(Sigma),ncol=1)
    sumvar<-sum(diag(Sigma))
    for (i in 1:nrow(Sigma)){
        empty[i]<-Sigma[i,i]/sumvar
    }
    return(empty)
}
tester1<-matrix(c(1,0,0,1),nrow=2)
ZCAprop(tester1)

tester2<-matrix(c(4,1,1,3),nrow=2)
ZCAprop(tester2)

tester3<-matrix(c(4,1,1,1,5,1,1,1,10),nrow=3)
ZCAprop(tester3)

ZCAcorprop<-function(Sigma){
    empty<-matrix(0,nrow=nrow(Sigma),ncol=1)
    for (i in 1:nrow(Sigma)){
        empty[i]<-nrow(Sigma)
    }
    return(empty)
}
tester1<-matrix(c(1,0,0,1),nrow=2)
ZCAcorprop(tester1)

tester2<-matrix(c(4,1,1,3),nrow=2)
ZCAcorprop(tester2)

tester3<-matrix(c(4,1,1,1,5,1,1,1,10),nrow=3)
ZCAcorprop(tester3)

PCAprop<-function(Sigma){
    eigenvalue<-eigen(Sigma)$values
    empty<-matrix(0,nrow=nrow(Sigma),ncol=1)
    for (i in 1:nrow(Sigma)){
        empty[i]<-eigenvalue[i]/sum(eigenvalue)
    }
    return(empty)
}
tester1<-matrix(c(1,0,0,1),nrow=2)
PCAprop(tester1)

tester2<-matrix(c(4,1,1,3),nrow=2)
PCAprop(tester2)

tester3<-matrix(c(4,1,1,1,5,1,1,1,10),nrow=3)
PCAprop(tester3)

PCAcorprop<-function(Sigma){
    temp<-findingP(Sigma,1)
    eigenvalue<-eigen(temp)$values
    empty<-matrix(0,nrow=nrow(Sigma),ncol=1)
    for (i in 1:nrow(Sigma)){
        empty[i]<-eigenvalue[i]/sum(eigenvalue)
    }
    return(empty)
}
tester1<-matrix(c(1,0,0,1),nrow=2)
PCAcorprop(tester1)

tester2<-matrix(c(4,1,1,3),nrow=2)
PCAcorprop(tester2)

tester3<-matrix(c(4,1,1,1,5,1,1,1,10),nrow=3)
PCAcorprop(tester3)
```
